text:
Maya (People Ops): Quick question 5 international dental clinic in Madrid is asking if Redwood can direct-bill for a root canal. They say they bill in EUR and want payment via EFT + an EOB with PHI redacted before giving the member a copy. Provider claim ref: 2026-INT-8421. Who owns the provider EFT flow and what docs do we need?

Liam (Benefits): We support direct-bill for major dental procedures but require a few items first: signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB) from the member, provider banking instructions (IBAN + SWIFT/BIC), provider tax registration or local equivalent, and an itemized invoice in EUR.

Jess (Finance): Also need provider identifier (NPI or local ID), and a scanned copy of the clinic's remittance form. For redaction: finance can redact SSN, exact DOB, and address on the EOB PDF, but we need written member consent to redact PHI and to assign benefits to the provider.

Maya (People Ops): The clinic asked for a template or checklist we can send them "so they know what to fill out". Can someone paste a short provider-facing template/email I can forward?

Liam (Benefits): Paste below 5 short email + attachments checklist you can forward:

---
To: billing@clinic.es
Subject: Redwood Inference 5 Direct-Billing Request for member [MemberName] (Claim 2026-INT-8421)

Hello,

Thank you for offering to direct-bill. To start processing international direct payment please provide the following scanned documents and files: 

1) Signed Assignment of Benefits (AOB) from the patient (PDF with signature). 
2) Patient-signed consent authorizing Redwood to redact PHI on the EOB if requested. 
3) Provider banking details: IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, account name, and remittance instructions. 
4) Provider tax registration / local business ID (scanned).
5) Itemized clinic invoice / billing form showing CPT/ICD codes (or local procedure codes), service dates, and amounts (in EUR).
6) Provider billing contact: name, billing email, phone.

Please indicate if you can accept payment in USD and provide USD remittance instructions if available to speed FX settlement. Send all materials to claims@redwood.com and reference Claim 2026-INT-8421.

Best regards,
Redwood Claims Team
---

Jess (Finance): Add short line for currency: "If billing in EUR please confirm the exact amount net of VAT or include VAT line item." That helps our AP team.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks 5 I'll send that. One follow-up: provider wants to know if we can redact "everything except CPT and amounts" on the EOB before sending it to the member. Is that permissible?

Liam (Benefits): We can redact identifiers (SSN, full DOB, member home address) but we must leave service dates, CPT/procedure codes, and charge amounts for audit/compliance. Member must consent to the redaction and assignment. If the clinic wants more aggressive redaction, we need written legal approval.

BenefitsBot: Automated notice: International-claims workflow triggered. Manual review required. Expected adjudication window 5-10 business days after complete docs received.

Jess (Finance): Operational timeline: once claims receives complete docs and AOB, finance validates banking (up to 3 business days) then schedules the transfer (5-7 business days typical for EUR via correspondent banks). If provider agrees to USD payment, transfers may clear faster in some corridors.

Maya (People Ops): Great, I'll forward the template and request the AOB + consent. I'll cc claims@redwood.com and update this thread when the clinic replies. Thanks :thumbsup:

Liam (Benefits): If provider pushes back on AOB wording, send them this short consent clause to include in the patient-signed form: "I assign payment for services to the provider and authorize Redwood Inference to transmit a redacted Explanation of Benefits to me as described above."

Maya (People Ops): Copying that into the email. Closing loop here for now.

(End of thread)
